children: The tech sector remained in the spotlight this week amid a persistent sell-off from investors and earnings reports from companies including Qualcomm and AMD.
The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index
closed in the green on Friday, leading a recovery from its worst day in more than a year. The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the last week are as follows:
Top Gainers:
Fiserv
First Solar
Corpay
Block
Jack Henry & Associates
Top Losers:
Lumentum
Seagate Technology
Marvell Technology
Western Digital
Sandisk
Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:
Qualcomm crash following Q4 results
Qualcomm
shares plunged after its smartphone chip revenue tumbled 26% in the
as rising memory prices weighed on handset demand.

The San Diego-based semiconductor offered mixed guidance that overshadowed results for the fiscal fourth quarter. For the period ending Sept. 27, Qualcomm said it earned an adjusted $2.17 per share as revenue fell 7% year-over-year to come in at $10.44B.
Wall Street analysts have lowered their price targets on the stock given margin pressures and continued Apple modem share losses as risks to its near-term outlook.
Marvell announces $115B all-stock deal for Lumentum
Following speculation that a deal could be announced soon, Marvell Technology
that it intends to acquire Lumentum
in an all-stock deal. The deal puts an enterprise value of $115B on Lumentum, or roughly $1,132 per share.
According to Bloomberg, before announcing the deal, CEOs of both Marvell and Lumentum asked Nvidia
CEO
on the proposed deal, following which Huang gave his blessing on the potential tie-up, as consolidation among crucial suppliers in the AI buildout could reduce bottlenecks.
AMD in focus after better-than-expected results, guidance
Advanced Micro Devices

closed nearly 4% higher in extended trading on Tuesday as the semiconductor giant reported third-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's forecast. This also led to Wall Street praising the company's data center strength.
Morgan Stanley analyst Joseph Moore said the company is taking advantage of stronger server market conditions and taking “meaningful” share from companies like Intel.
AMD also recorded a third-quarter charge of more than $1B tied to the performance-based stock warrants it issued to major AI customers OpenAI
and Meta Platforms
. The chipmaker struck deals with OpenAI and Meta, agreeing to supply them chips in exchange for warrants that could let them buy up to 10% ​of AMD if it meets certain milestones.
However, the stock closed over 17% lower on Thursday following a broader tech sell-off.
Micron Technology plunges amid chip selloff, Taiwan plant halt
Micron Technology

has suspended plans for a memory chip plant in Taiwan amid a prolonged labor dispute, raising uncertainty over a major production base for components used in artificial intelligence systems, Bloomberg reported.

Micron dropped more than 17% on Thursday amid a sweeping semiconductor and AI-stock selloff, with reports linking the broader weakness to investor concerns about political scrutiny potentially slowing data-center development and infrastructure spending.
In other news,
Cisco
was downgraded to Equal-Weight from Overweight at Morgan Stanley on Thursday, as the investment firm said concerns are growing ahead of the networking giant's earnings, set to be released on Nov. 12.
HP
disclosed that it has appointed former GSK
CEO Emma Walmsley as its new CEO. Walmsley will take over for interim CEO Bruce Broussard, who has been in the top spot since February.
